MOLECULAR GENETICS LABORATORY REPORT
[redacted location] Medical Center

Patient: [redacted name]
MRN: [redacted ID]
DOB: [redacted date]
Specimen Type: Peripheral Blood
Collection Date: [redacted date]
Report Date: [redacted date]

CLINICAL INDICATION
Evaluation for possible sex chromosome abnormalities, specifically Klinefelter syndrome

TEST PERFORMED
Quantitative Fluorescence Polymerase Chain Reaction (QF-PCR) for Sex Chromosome Analysis

METHODOLOGY
DNA was extracted from peripheral blood. QF-PCR analysis was performed using fluorescently labeled primers for multiple polymorphic markers on the X and Y chromosomes. The following markers were analyzed:
- X chromosome: AMELX, DXS6809, DXS6803, DXS8377, HPRT
- Y chromosome: AMELY, SRY, DYS448, DYS391

Peak areas and ratios were calculated to determine chromosome copy number.

RESULTS
X chromosome markers: Single allele peaks detected, consistent with one X chromosome
Y chromosome markers: Present with normal peak heights
SRY gene: Detected at expected location on Yp11.31
AMEL X:Y ratio: 1:1

INTERPRETATION
Results are consistent with a normal male sex chromosome complement (46,XY). The presence of the SRY gene sequence on Yp11.31 confirms normal Y chromosome structure. Klinefelter syndrome (47,XXY) is excluded based on these findings.

TEST LIMITATIONS
This test is designed to detect common sex chromosome aneuploidies. Low-level mosaicism (<20%) may not be detected. Structural rearrangements or segmental imbalances that do not affect marker regions will not be identified by this methodology.

RECOMMENDATIONS
Array CGH analysis is pending and will provide additional information regarding submicroscopic chromosomal imbalances.

Reported by: [redacted name], PhD
Laboratory Director: [redacted name], MD, PhD
